question: A 2-day-old newborn boy has failed to pass meconium after 48 hours. There is an absence of stool in the rectal vault. Family history is significant for MEN2A syndrome. Which of the following confirms the diagnosis?

options.opa: Absence of ganglion cells demonstrated by rectal suction biopsy
options.opb: Atrophic nerve fibers and decreased acetylcholinesterase activity
options.opc: Barium enema demonstrating absence of a transition zone
options.opd: Rectal manometry demonstrating relaxation of the internal anal sphincter with distension of the rectum
options.ope: Genetic testing confirming mutation in the RET oncogene

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Absence of meconium after 48 hours in a 2-day-old newborn boy -> Suspected Hirschsprung disease -> 70% CHAIN: Family history significant for MEN2A syndrome -> Consideration of possible association with Hirschsprung disease -> 60% CHAIN: Hirschsprung disease suspected -> Diagnostic tests required for confirmation -> 80% CHAIN: Absence of ganglion cells demonstrated by rectal suction biopsy -> Confirmatory for Hirschsprung disease -> 95% CHAIN: Genetic testing confirming mutation in the RET oncogene -> Confirms MEN2A syndrome -> 70%
enhanced_information: The absence of ganglion cells demonstrated by rectal suction biopsy confirms the diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease in this 2-day-old newborn boy. Genetic testing confirming a mutation in the RET oncogene would confirm MEN2A syndrome. The rectal suction biopsy is crucial for diagnosing Hirschsprung disease, while genetic testing is essential for confirming MEN2A syndrome.
analysis: The core medical principle here is to differentiate between Hirschsprung disease and MEN2A syndrome. In this case, the absence of ganglion cells demonstrated by rectal suction biopsy confirms the diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease, not MEN2A syndrome. Genetic testing confirming a mutation in the RET oncogene would confirm MEN2A syndrome. Given the context provided, the rectal suction biopsy showing the absence of ganglion cells is the most appropriate diagnostic test for the current presentation.
